questions.stimulus: A company develops a voice recognition system for customer service calls. The development team consists entirely of native English speakers from the same region of the United States.
questions.question: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of the team's composition?

options.A: The system will not be able to process audio input because the team lacked audio engineers
options.B: The system may perform poorly for users with different accents or dialects because those perspectives were not represented during development
options.C: The system will work correctly for all users because voice recognition technology is accent-neutral
options.D: The system will contain more syntax errors because a homogeneous team communicates less effectively

questions.explanation: Collaboration that includes diverse perspectives helps avoid bias. A team of native English speakers from one region is unlikely to anticipate the needs of users with different accents or dialects, resulting in a biased system.

questions.stimulus: A company develops a voice recognition system for customer service calls. The development team consists entirely of native English speakers from the same region of the United States.
questions.question: Which of the following actions would MOST directly address the limitation described?

options.A: Expanding the team to include more native English speakers from other regions
options.B: Consulting with potential users who speak different languages and dialects during development
options.C: Using pair programming to have two developers review all code simultaneously
options.D: Using online collaboration tools so team members can share feedback more efficiently

questions.explanation: Information gathered from potential users can be used to understand the purpose of a program from diverse perspectives. Consulting users who speak different languages and dialects would directly address the bias in the system.

questions.question: A student is classifying the following items as computing innovations or not: a smart insulin pump, a printed cookbook, and a ride-sharing service. Which of the following correctly classifies all three?

options.A: All three are computing innovations because they all help people accomplish tasks
options.B: Only the smart insulin pump is a computing innovation because it is the only physical device with embedded technology
options.C: The smart insulin pump and ride-sharing service are computing innovations; the printed cookbook is not
options.D: The ride-sharing service is not a computing innovation because it involves human drivers rather than automated systems

questions.explanation: A computing innovation must include a program as an integral part of its function. A smart insulin pump and ride-sharing service both require programs to function. A printed cookbook does not include a program.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a nonphysical computing concept?

options.A: A fitness tracking app installed on a smartphone
options.B: A smart thermostat that learns user temperature preferences
options.C: A social media platform that connects users across the world
options.D: A photo editing program that applies filters to images

questions.explanation: A nonphysical computing concept is a system or model enabled by computing. A social media platform is a system enabled by computing. A fitness app and photo editing program are nonphysical software. A smart thermostat is a physical innovation.

questions.stimulus: Two programmers are working together on a complex module. Programmer A writes code while Programmer B watches, asks questions, and points out potential issues in real time. After completing the module, they switch roles for the next task.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the collaboration model being used?

options.A: Iterative development, because the programmers repeatedly refine the same code
options.B: Pair programming, because one programmer writes while the other observes and provides feedback
options.C: Distributed computing, because the two programmers divide the work between two machines
options.D: Modular design, because the programmers break the program into separate modules

questions.explanation: Pair programming is a recognized collaboration model where one programmer writes code while another observes and provides real-time feedback. The switching of roles is consistent with this model.

questions.stimulus: Two programmers are working together on a complex module. Programmer A writes code while Programmer B watches, asks questions, and points out potential issues in real time. After completing the module, they switch roles for the next task.
questions.question: Programmer A argues that Programmer B is not contributing because Programmer B is not writing any code. Which of the following best refutes this claim?

options.A: Programmer B contributes by documenting the code after it is written
options.B: Programmer B contributes by testing the code after the module is complete
options.C: Programmer B actively contributes by catching errors and providing feedback that improves the code in real time
options.D: Programmer B contributes by managing the project timeline while Programmer A focuses on coding

questions.explanation: In pair programming both roles actively contribute. The observer's real-time feedback is a core contribution of the model — catching errors the writer might miss is distinct from testing or documentation which happen after writing.

questions.stimulus: A development team building a navigation app for cyclists uses an online platform where members post code updates, leave comments on each other's work, and suggest improvements asynchronously across different time zones.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes how the team's approach supports collaboration?

options.A: The online platform eliminates the need for the team to practice interpersonal skills because communication is automated
options.B: The online platform allows the team to share code and provide feedback regardless of location or time zone
options.C: The online platform ensures all team members write the same amount of code
options.D: The online platform replaces the need for pair programming by allowing two people to edit the same file

questions.explanation: Online tools support collaboration by allowing programmers to share and provide feedback on ideas and documents. The key benefit described is asynchronous collaboration across locations and time zones.

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains ONLY the interpersonal skills identified as essential for effective collaborative teams?

options.A: Communication, pair programming, conflict resolution, and negotiation
options.B: Communication, consensus building, conflict resolution, and negotiation
options.C: Brainstorming, consensus building, conflict resolution, and user consultation
options.D: Communication, consensus building, iterative development, and negotiation

questions.explanation: Communication, consensus building, conflict resolution, and negotiation are the four interpersonal skills identified for effective collaborative teams. The other options each include a process or model that is not an interpersonal skill.

questions.stimulus: A team is developing a translation app. Before finalizing the design, they survey speakers of 12 different languages, interview immigrants and international students, and conduct usability sessions with non-native speakers of varying fluency levels.
questions.question: Which of the following best explains the purpose of the team's user research approach?

options.A: To identify syntax errors in the app before the coding phase begins
options.B: To ensure the app meets legal requirements for serving international users
options.C: To gather information from potential users so the app can be developed to fully incorporate diverse perspectives
options.D: To replace pair programming with a more efficient feedback method

questions.explanation: Information gathered from potential users can be used to understand the purpose of a program from diverse perspectives and to develop a program that fully incorporates those perspectives.

questions.question: A team develops an automated resume screening tool trained on hiring data from the past 15 years. After deployment, the tool consistently ranks candidates from certain universities significantly higher than equally qualified candidates from other schools. Which TWO of the following best explain this outcome?

options.A: The tool contains a syntax error that causes it to misread university names
options.B: The historical data used to train the tool reflected past hiring preferences, embedding that bias into the tool
options.C: The development team did not include diverse perspectives that might have identified the bias before deployment
options.D: The tool was not tested with enough candidates, causing it to default to random rankings

questions.explanation: The bias comes from two sources: the historical data that reflected past biased hiring practices (B), and the lack of diverse perspectives on the development team that would have identified and questioned that bias before deployment (C).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a computing innovation?

options.A: A streaming music service that recommends songs based on listening history
options.B: A mechanical clock that displays the time using gears and springs
options.C: A smart refrigerator that orders groceries automatically when items run low
options.D: An online tutoring platform that connects students with teachers

questions.explanation: A computing innovation must include a program as an integral part of its function. A mechanical clock operates entirely through physical mechanisms with no program involved. All other options require programs to function.

questions.question: A developer is building a budgeting app. They argue that consulting potential users is unnecessary because they personally use budgeting apps and understand what users need. Which of the following best evaluates this reasoning?

options.A: The developer is correct because firsthand experience with budgeting apps is sufficient to understand all user needs
options.B: The developer is incorrect because one person's experience cannot represent the diverse perspectives of all potential users
options.C: The developer is correct because consulting users adds time to development without improving the final product
options.D: The developer is incorrect because only professional financial advisors should be consulted when building budgeting apps

questions.explanation: Information gathered from potential users helps understand the program's purpose from diverse perspectives. One developer's experience represents only a single perspective and cannot capture the full range of needs of a diverse user base.

questions.stimulus:
ActivityDescription
Activity 1Team members use a shared repository to upload code and comment on each other's contributions
Activity 2One programmer types while another reads along and suggests changes in real time
Activity 3The team holds a meeting to resolve a disagreement about the app's design
Activity 4The team surveys 500 potential users before finalizing the app's features
questions.question: Which activity is an example of using online tools to support collaboration?

options.A: Activity 1
options.B: Activity 2
options.C: Activity 3
options.D: Activity 4

questions.explanation: Online tools support collaboration by allowing programmers to share and provide feedback on ideas and documents. A shared repository where team members upload code and comment on contributions is an example of an online collaboration tool.

questions.stimulus:
ActivityDescription
Activity 1Team members use a shared repository to upload code and comment on each other's contributions
Activity 2One programmer types while another reads along and suggests changes in real time
Activity 3The team holds a meeting to resolve a disagreement about the app's design
Activity 4The team surveys 500 potential users before finalizing the app's features
questions.question: Which activity best demonstrates the interpersonal skill of conflict resolution?

options.A: Activity 1
options.B: Activity 2
options.C: Activity 3
options.D: Activity 4

questions.explanation: Conflict resolution is one of the interpersonal skills practiced by effective collaborative teams. Holding a meeting specifically to resolve a disagreement directly demonstrates conflict resolution.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform allows customers to browse products, add items to a cart, and complete purchases online. Which type of computing innovation is this?

options.A: Physical computing innovation, because customers interact with physical products
options.B: Nonphysical computing software, because it is a standalone application
options.C: Nonphysical computing concept, because it is a system or model enabled by computing
options.D: Physical computing innovation, because it requires servers to operate

questions.explanation: A nonphysical computing concept is a system or model enabled by computing rather than a physical device or standalone software. E-commerce is a business model that exists because of computing.

questions.stimulus: A startup is building a language learning app. After six months of development, a team member suggests holding user testing sessions with non-native speakers before the app launches. Other team members argue this will delay the launch.
questions.question: Which of the following best supports holding the user testing sessions?

options.A: User testing will ensure the app has no syntax errors before launch
options.B: Non-native speakers are the target users and their feedback will help the app fully incorporate their perspectives
options.C: User testing will allow the team to practice pair programming before launch
options.D: Non-native speakers can help the team write better documentation for the app

questions.explanation: Information gathered from potential users helps develop a program that fully incorporates their perspectives. Since non-native speakers are the target audience, their feedback directly improves the app's ability to serve its users.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why effective collaboration is different from simply working in a group?

options.A: Collaboration requires more team members than group work
options.B: Collaboration requires the use of online tools while group work does not
options.C: Collaboration requires equal participation and voice from all members while group work does not necessarily ensure this
options.D: Collaboration is only possible when team members are in the same physical location

questions.explanation: Effective collaboration requires equal participation and voice from all members of the group — this is what distinguishes it from simply working in a group where some members may dominate or others may not contribute.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of nonphysical computing software?

options.A: A smart pacemaker that monitors heart rhythm
options.B: A word processing application
options.C: A social media platform
options.D: A photo editing program

questions.explanation: Nonphysical computing software refers to standalone software applications. A word processing application and photo editing program are both standalone software applications. A smart pacemaker is a physical innovation. A social media platform is a nonphysical computing concept.

questions.question: A student creates a program that displays a different greeting depending on the time of day. Which of the following best describes the purpose of this program?

options.A: To store data about the user's preferences in a database
options.B: To solve a problem or pursue an interest through creative expression
options.C: To test whether the computer's clock is functioning correctly
options.D: To demonstrate the use of variables in a programming language

questions.explanation: The purpose of computing innovations is to solve problems or pursue interests through creative expression. A personalized greeting program pursues the interest of providing a customized user experience.

questions.stimulus: A weather app accepts a city name as input and displays the current temperature, humidity, and forecast for that city.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes an event in this program?

options.A: The temperature value stored in the program's memory
options.B: The forecast data retrieved from a weather database
options.C: The user tapping the Search button after typing a city name
options.D: The list of cities the program can retrieve weather data for

questions.explanation: An event is associated with an action and supplies input data to a program. The user tapping the Search button is the action that triggers the program to process the city name input.

questions.stimulus: A weather app accepts a city name as input and displays the current temperature, humidity, and forecast for that city.
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of program output produced by this app?

options.A: The current temperature displayed on screen
options.B: The city name typed by the user
options.C: The humidity percentage shown to the user
options.D: The forecast text displayed after the search

questions.explanation: Program outputs are data sent from a program to a device. The city name typed by the user is program input. The temperature, humidity, and forecast are all outputs sent from the program to the user's screen.

questions.question: A programmer is designing a calculator app. The app must correctly handle all possible numeric inputs including very large numbers, decimals, and negative numbers. Which of the following best explains why this requirement exists?

options.A: A program must be written in a language that supports all numeric types
options.B: A program needs to work for a variety of inputs and situations
options.C: A program's output must always be a number when the input is a number
options.D: A program must store all previous inputs in memory for future reference

questions.explanation: A program needs to work for a variety of inputs and situations. A calculator that only works for some numeric inputs would be incomplete.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between a program and a code segment?

options.A: A program is written by one person while a code segment is written collaboratively
options.B: A program performs a complete task when run while a code segment is a collection of statements that is part of a larger program
options.C: A program runs on a computer while a code segment runs on a mobile device
options.D: A program uses variables while a code segment uses only constants

questions.explanation: A program is a collection of program statements that performs a specific task when run. A code segment is a collection of statements that is part of a larger program.

questions.question: A music app plays a song when a user taps a play button and pauses it when the user taps again. Which of the following best describes the programming style used?

options.A: Sequential programming, because the app executes statements in order from top to bottom
options.B: Iterative programming, because the app repeats the same action each time the button is tapped
options.C: Event-driven programming, because program statements execute when triggered by a user action rather than through sequential flow
options.D: Modular programming, because the play and pause functions are separated into different modules

questions.explanation: In event-driven programming, program statements are executed when triggered rather than through sequential flow of control. The user tapping the play button is the event that triggers execution.

questions.question: A navigation app takes a starting location and destination as input and displays a route on a map. Which TWO of the following are examples of program input for this app?

options.A: The map displayed on the user's screen
options.B: The estimated travel time shown after the route is calculated
options.C: The destination address typed by the user
options.D: The user's current GPS location detected by the device

questions.explanation: Program inputs are data sent to a computer for processing. The destination address (C) and GPS location (D) are both inputs. The map display and travel time are outputs sent from the program to the user's screen.

questions.question: A programmer describes their app by saying 'it takes a photo as input and applies a vintage filter to produce a new image as output.' Which of the following best describes this type of description?

options.A: A detailed description because it explains both what the program does and how the statements accomplish this
options.B: A broad description because it describes what the program does without explaining how the program statements work
options.C: A program specification because it defines all the requirements for the program
options.D: A code segment because it describes a portion of the program's functionality

questions.explanation: A program can be described broadly by what it does, or in more detail by both what it does and how its statements accomplish this. Describing input and output without explaining the underlying statements is a broad description.

questions.stimulus: A smart thermostat automatically adjusts the temperature based on the time of day, the current temperature reading from its sensors, and schedules set by the user.
questions.question: Which of the following best identifies all the inputs to this program?

options.A: The adjusted temperature displayed on the thermostat screen
options.B: The time of day, current temperature from sensors, and user-set schedules
options.C: The heating and cooling commands sent to the HVAC system
options.D: The time of day only, because user schedules are stored internally not sent as input

questions.explanation: Program inputs are data sent to a computer for processing. The time of day, sensor readings, and user schedules are all data sent to the thermostat's program for processing. The displayed temperature and HVAC commands are outputs.

questions.question: A program that converts temperatures from Celsius to Fahrenheit produces correct results for 0°C and 100°C but gives wrong answers for negative temperatures. Which of the following best explains this situation?

options.A: The program has a syntax error that only appears for negative inputs
options.B: The program does not work for a variety of inputs and situations as required
options.C: The program has an overflow error because negative numbers exceed the defined range
options.D: The program is working correctly because most temperatures are not negative

questions.explanation: A program needs to work for a variety of inputs and situations. A temperature converter that fails for negative inputs is incomplete — it must handle all valid temperature values.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of input that comes from another program rather than a user?

options.A: A user typing a search query into a search engine
options.B: A user tapping a button to submit a form
options.C: A weather app receiving current temperature data from an online weather service
options.D: A user speaking a voice command to a virtual assistant

questions.explanation: Input can come from a user or other programs. A weather app receiving data from an online weather service is an example of input coming from another program rather than direct user interaction.

questions.stimulus: A fitness app displays the number of steps taken, calories burned, and a motivational message each time the user taps the Refresh button.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the output of this program?

options.A: The user tapping the Refresh button
options.B: The step count data collected by the phone's motion sensor
options.C: The steps taken, calories burned, and motivational message displayed to the user
options.D: The fitness goals entered by the user when setting up the app

questions.explanation: Program outputs are any data sent from a program to a device. The steps taken, calories burned, and motivational message are all data sent from the program to the user's screen.

questions.question: A developer better understands that their note-taking app's purpose is to help students organize ideas quickly during lectures. Which of the following best explains how this understanding helps the developer?

options.A: It allows the developer to write more efficient code with fewer lines
options.B: It provides the developer with an improved ability to develop the app by knowing what features and behaviors to prioritize
options.C: It eliminates the need to consult with users because the purpose is already defined
options.D: It allows the developer to skip the testing phase because the purpose is clear

questions.explanation: An understanding of the purpose of a computing innovation provides developers with an improved ability to develop that innovation. Knowing users need to organize ideas quickly during lectures tells the developer to prioritize speed and simplicity.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are examples of events that can trigger program execution?

options.A: A variable being assigned a new value inside the program
options.B: A user pressing a key on the keyboard
options.C: A program finishing its execution and closing
options.D: A mouse click on a button in the user interface

questions.explanation: Events can be generated when a key is pressed, a mouse is clicked, a program is started, or any other defined action occurs that affects the flow of execution. A key press and mouse click are both events. Variable assignment is internal program execution, not an event.

questions.stimulus: A team is developing a fitness tracking app. They release a basic version, gather user feedback, redesign the step-counting feature based on complaints, release an updated version, gather more feedback, and repeat the process several times over six months.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the development process being used?

options.A: Incremental development, because the team adds new features with each release
options.B: Iterative development, because the team refines and revises the program based on feedback throughout the process
options.C: Sequential development, because the team follows the same steps in the same order each time
options.D: Pair programming, because two developers review each update before it is released

questions.explanation: A development process that is iterative requires refinement and revision based on feedback throughout the process. The team repeatedly revises based on user feedback.

questions.stimulus: A team is building a social media app. They complete and fully test the login system before beginning work on the profile page. Once the profile page works correctly they begin building the feed. They do not start a new feature until the previous one is verified to work.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the development process being used?

options.A: Iterative development, because the team revisits each feature multiple times
options.B: Exploratory development, because the team does not plan ahead before building each feature
options.C: Incremental development, because the team builds and verifies one piece at a time before adding the next
options.D: Modular development, because the team separates the app into independent modules

questions.explanation: A development process that is incremental breaks the problem into smaller pieces and makes sure each piece works before adding it to the whole.

questions.question: A team is in the investigation phase of developing a new ride-sharing app. Which of the following activities is LEAST consistent with this phase?

options.A: Conducting interviews with frequent ride-sharing users
options.B: Observing how people currently use competing apps
options.C: Writing the code for the payment processing module
options.D: Surveying potential users about their biggest frustrations with existing services

questions.explanation: Investigation methods include surveys, interviews, and direct observations. Writing code belongs to the prototyping phase, not the investigation phase.

questions.question: A programmer adds the following note directly into their code: '# This function calculates the total price including tax'. Which of the following best describes this note?

options.A: A variable that stores the function's return value
options.B: A comment that documents the function's purpose and does not affect how the program runs
options.C: A test case used to verify the function produces the correct output
options.D: A specification that defines the requirements for the program

questions.explanation: Comments are a form of program documentation written into the program to be read by people and do not affect how a program runs.

questions.stimulus: A programmer finds a sorting algorithm online and uses it in their program. They add the following line to their documentation: 'Sorting function adapted from quicksort implementation by J. Smith, available at codeexamples.com'.
questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the programmer added this line?

options.A: To explain how the sorting algorithm works so other programmers can understand the code
options.B: To acknowledge code that was written by another source, as required when using code developed by others
options.C: To document a test case that verifies the sorting function works correctly
options.D: To describe the program specification that required a sorting feature

questions.explanation: It is important to acknowledge any code segments developed by another source. The acknowledgement should be in the program documentation and include the origin or original author's name.

questions.question: Which of the following activities belongs in the DESIGN phase of program development?

options.A: Conducting user interviews to understand the program's requirements
options.B: Running the program with test inputs to check for errors
options.C: Creating diagrams that represent the layout of the user interface
options.D: Releasing a working version of the program to gather user feedback

questions.explanation: The design phase may include brainstorming, planning, organizing into modules, creation of UI layout diagrams, and development of a testing strategy. User interviews are investigation, running tests is testing, and releasing to users is prototyping.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are effective methods of investigation during the development of a new program?

options.A: Writing comments that explain what each code segment does
options.B: Conducting surveys to collect data from potential users
options.C: Organizing the program into separate modules and functional components
options.D: Directly observing how people currently perform the task the program will automate

questions.explanation: Investigation methods include collecting data through surveys and direct observations. Writing comments is documentation and organizing into modules belongs to the design phase.

questions.stimulus: A team develops a hospital scheduling app. Before writing any code, they create wireframe sketches of every screen, map out how users will navigate between pages, and divide the app into a login module, scheduling module, and notification module.
questions.question: Which phase of development is the team currently in?

options.A: Investigation, because they are gathering information about user needs
options.B: Prototyping, because they are creating early versions of the app's screens
options.C: Design, because they are planning the structure and layout of the program before coding
options.D: Testing, because they are checking whether the navigation works correctly

questions.explanation: The design phase includes brainstorming, planning and storyboarding, organizing the program into modules, and creating diagrams that represent user interface layouts. The team is doing exactly this before writing any code.

questions.question: A programmer writes detailed comments throughout their code as they develop each function. A teammate argues this is a waste of time and comments should be written after the program is complete. Which of the following best evaluates this disagreement?

options.A: The teammate is correct because comments do not affect program execution and can always be added later
options.B: The programmer is correct because programmers should document throughout development, not just at the end
options.C: The teammate is correct because writing comments during development slows down coding and increases errors
options.D: The programmer is correct because comments written during development automatically become the program specification

questions.explanation: Programmers should document a program throughout its development — not just at the end. Documentation written during development is more accurate and helps maintain correct programs individually and collaboratively.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of program documentation?

options.A: To make the program run faster by explaining the algorithm to the compiler
options.B: To describe the function of code segments and how they were developed, helping programmers develop and maintain correct programs
options.C: To replace the need for testing by providing a written record of expected behavior
options.D: To satisfy legal requirements for programs that handle user data

questions.explanation: Program documentation is a written description of the function of a code segment, event, procedure, or program and how it was developed. It helps in developing and maintaining correct programs individually and in collaborative environments.

questions.question: A programming environment does not support comments. Which of the following best describes how a programmer should handle documentation in this environment?

options.A: The programmer does not need to document the program since comments are unavailable
options.B: The programmer should use other methods of documentation since not all programming environments support comments
options.C: The programmer should switch to a different programming environment that supports comments
options.D: The programmer should add documentation only after the program is complete and exported

questions.explanation: Not all programming environments support comments, so other methods of documentation may be required. The need for documentation does not go away just because the environment does not support comments.

questions.stimulus: A team is developing a new social media app. They begin by interviewing teenagers about how they currently use social media and what frustrates them. They then define the app's requirements based on these interviews before designing or building anything.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes what the team is doing and why?

options.A: Testing, to verify the app meets user needs before launching
options.B: Investigation, to understand user constraints and concerns before defining requirements
options.C: Design, to plan the app's features based on what teenagers want
options.D: Prototyping, to create an early version of the app for teenagers to try

questions.explanation: Investigation in a development process is useful for understanding and identifying program constraints, as well as the concerns and interests of the people who will use the program. Interviewing users before defining requirements is investigation.

questions.question: A team finishes building a program and realizes they used a sorting algorithm they found in a textbook without citing it. Which of the following best describes what the team should do?

options.A: Nothing, because algorithms cannot be copyrighted and do not need to be cited
options.B: Add an acknowledgement in the program documentation that includes the textbook as the source
options.C: Rewrite the algorithm from scratch so they do not need to acknowledge the source
options.D: Add the citation only if the textbook's author requests credit

questions.explanation: It is important to acknowledge any code segments written by someone else. The acknowledgement should be in the program documentation and include the origin or original author's name.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between a program's requirements and its specification?

options.A: Requirements describe how the program will be coded while the specification describes what it will do
options.B: Requirements describe how the program functions and user interactions it must provide while the specification defines those requirements formally
options.C: Requirements are written by users while the specification is written by developers
options.D: Requirements are created during the design phase while the specification is created during testing

questions.explanation: Program requirements describe how a program functions and may include user interactions it must provide. A program's specification defines those requirements formally. The design phase then outlines how to accomplish the specification.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following best describe characteristics of iterative development?

options.A: The team builds and verifies one feature completely before starting the next
options.B: The development process may require revisiting earlier phases based on feedback
options.C: Refinement and revision based on testing or reflection occur throughout the process
options.D: The development process always follows the same fixed sequence of phases without looping back

questions.explanation: Iterative development requires refinement and revision based on feedback, testing, or reflection throughout the process, and may require revisiting earlier phases. Building one feature at a time before starting the next describes incremental development.

questions.stimulus: A programmer writes a program that is intended to calculate the average of a list of numbers. When run with the input [10, 20, 30], the program displays 25 instead of 20.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the type of error in this program?

options.A: Syntax error, because the program does not follow the rules of the programming language
options.B: Run-time error, because the program crashes when given this input
options.C: Overflow error, because the numbers exceed the defined range of values
options.D: Logic error, because the program runs but produces an incorrect result

questions.explanation: A logic error is a mistake in the algorithm or program that causes it to behave incorrectly or unexpectedly. The program runs without crashing but produces the wrong answer.

questions.stimulus:
result ← 10 + 5
DISPLAY rezult
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the error in this code segment?

options.A: Logic error, because the calculation produces the wrong result
options.B: Run-time error, because the program will crash when it reaches the DISPLAY statement
options.C: Syntax error, because the variable name rezult does not match the variable result that was defined
options.D: Overflow error, because the result of 10 + 5 exceeds the defined range of values

questions.explanation: A syntax error is a mistake where the rules of the programming language are not followed. Using rezult instead of result violates the rule that variable names must be consistent.

questions.question: A program that divides two numbers crashes when the user enters 0 as the denominator. Which of the following best describes this type of error?

options.A: Logic error, because dividing by zero produces an incorrect mathematical result
options.B: Syntax error, because division by zero violates the rules of the programming language
options.C: Run-time error, because the error occurs during the execution of the program
options.D: Overflow error, because zero is outside the defined range of values for a denominator

questions.explanation: A run-time error is a mistake that occurs during execution. Division by zero does not prevent the program from starting but causes it to crash when that line executes.

questions.stimulus: A programmer is trying to find an error in a procedure that calculates shipping costs. She manually traces through each line of the code using a specific test input, tracking the value of each variable at each step.
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the error-finding technique being used?

options.A: Adding extra output statements to print variable values during execution
options.B: Using a debugger to pause execution at specific lines
options.C: Hand tracing, by manually tracking variable values through each step of the code
options.D: Using a test case to compare expected and actual output

questions.explanation: Hand tracing involves manually stepping through the code and tracking variable values at each step. The programmer is hand tracing, not using a debugger or test case.

questions.question: A programmer is testing a program that accepts a user's age as input and must work correctly for all valid ages. Which of the following sets of test inputs would be MOST effective for verifying the program works correctly?
questions.explanation: Defined inputs used to test a program should demonstrate expected outcomes at or just beyond the extremes of input data. Testing with boundary values (0, 1 for minimum and 99, 100 for maximum) is most effective for catching edge case errors.

questions.question: A program that tracks a company's annual revenue stores the value as an integer. At the end of a record-breaking year, the program suddenly displays a negative revenue figure even though all individual transactions were positive. Which of the following best explains this behavior?

options.A: A logic error caused the program to subtract transactions instead of adding them
options.B: A syntax error caused the program to misread the transaction data
options.C: An overflow error occurred because the revenue value exceeded the defined range of values for the integer type
options.D: A run-time error caused the program to crash and reset the revenue to a negative default value

questions.explanation: An overflow error occurs when a computer attempts to handle a number outside the defined range of values. When an integer exceeds its maximum value it wraps around to a negative number, which explains the unexpected negative result.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are effective ways to find and correct errors in a program?

options.A: Adding extra output statements to display variable values at key points during execution
options.B: Rewriting the program in a different programming language
options.C: Using a debugger to pause execution and inspect variable values
options.D: Increasing the number of programmers working on the program

questions.explanation: Adding extra output statements and using debuggers are both identified as effective ways to find and correct errors. Rewriting in a different language does not fix logic errors, and adding more programmers does not directly help identify existing errors.

questions.question: A program is intended to find the largest number in a list. When given the list [3, 7, 2, 9, 4], the program returns 7 instead of 9. The program does not crash. Which of the following best describes this error?

options.A: Syntax error, because the program is not following the rules of the language correctly
options.B: Run-time error, because the program produces an unexpected result during execution
options.C: Logic error, because the algorithm is incorrect and causes the program to behave unexpectedly
options.D: Overflow error, because the list contains more values than the program can handle

questions.explanation: A logic error is a mistake in the algorithm or program that causes it to behave incorrectly or unexpectedly. The program runs without crashing but produces the wrong answer.

questions.stimulus:
x ← 10
y ← 0
z ← x / y
DISPLAY z
questions.question: Which of the following best describes what happens when this code segment is executed?

options.A: A syntax error occurs because dividing by a variable is not allowed
options.B: A logic error occurs because the result of dividing by zero is mathematically undefined
options.C: A run-time error occurs because the program attempts to divide by zero during execution
options.D: An overflow error occurs because zero is outside the defined range of integer values

questions.explanation: A run-time error is a mistake in the program that occurs during execution. Division by zero causes the program to fail when that specific line executes — it is a run-time error because the code was syntactically valid but fails during execution.

questions.question: The procedure is intended to return the price after applying a discount. Which of the following best describes the error?

options.A: Syntax error, because the procedure is missing a closing bracket
options.B: Logic error, because the procedure adds the discount amount instead of subtracting it
options.C: Run-time error, because the procedure will crash when discountRate is 0
options.D: Overflow error, because multiplying price and discountRate may produce a very large number

questions.explanation: A logic error is a mistake in the algorithm that causes it to behave incorrectly. The procedure adds the discount amount to the price instead of subtracting it — the program runs but produces incorrect results.

questions.question: A programmer adds the line DISPLAY count to their code at several points to track how the variable count changes as the program runs. Which of the following best describes this technique?

options.A: Hand tracing, because the programmer is manually stepping through the code
options.B: Adding extra output statements, because the programmer is inserting display commands to track variable values during execution
options.C: Using a debugger, because the programmer is pausing execution to inspect the variable
options.D: Using a test case, because the programmer is checking whether count matches the expected value

questions.explanation: Adding extra output statements is an effective way to find and correct errors. Inserting DISPLAY commands to track how a variable changes during execution is exactly this technique.

questions.question: A programmer is testing a program that calculates shipping costs based on package weight. The program should work for all valid weights from 0.1 kg to 50 kg. Which of the following sets of test inputs would be MOST effective?
questions.explanation: Test inputs should demonstrate different expected outcomes at or just beyond the extremes of input data. Testing 0 and 51 (just beyond the valid range) alongside 0.1 and 50 (the exact boundaries) and a middle value is the most effective strategy for catching edge case errors.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why program requirements are needed to identify appropriate test inputs?

options.A: Requirements specify the programming language which determines what inputs are valid
options.B: Requirements describe how the program functions and what user interactions it must provide, which defines what inputs and expected outputs should be tested
options.C: Requirements list all possible inputs that users might enter so testers know which ones to try
options.D: Requirements are written by users who already know which inputs cause the most errors

questions.explanation: Program requirements are needed to identify appropriate defined inputs for testing because requirements describe how the program functions and the user interactions it must provide — this tells developers what behavior to verify and what inputs to use.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following describe characteristics of a syntax error?

options.A: The program runs but produces an incorrect result
options.B: The program cannot run until the error is corrected
options.C: The error occurs because the rules of the programming language were not followed
options.D: The error only appears when the program is given certain inputs

questions.explanation: A syntax error is a mistake where the rules of the programming language are not followed, and the program cannot run until the error is corrected. A program that runs but produces wrong results has a logic error. An error that appears only with certain inputs is a run-time or logic error.

questions.question: A programmer uses a tool that allows them to pause the program at any line, inspect the values of all variables at that moment, and step through the code one line at a time. Which of the following best describes this tool?

options.A: A test case, because the programmer is using specific inputs to check the program
options.B: A visualization, because the tool displays the program's state graphically
options.C: A debugger, because the tool pauses execution and allows inspection of variable values
options.D: An extra output statement, because the tool displays variable values during execution

questions.explanation: A debugger is an effective way to find and correct errors — it allows programmers to pause execution at specific points and inspect variable values. This is distinct from extra output statements which print values without pausing execution.

questions.stimulus: A student created a program that helps users track their daily water intake. The program accepts the number of ounces of water the user drank as input and displays a message telling the user whether they met their daily goal of 64 ounces.
questions.question: Identify one valid input to this program and describe what the program does with that input.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for identifying a valid numeric input (e.g. 50 ounces, 70 ounces, 0 ounces).
Award 1 point for correctly describing what the program does with the input — it compares the input to the goal of 64 ounces and displays a message indicating whether the goal was met.
Example: An input of 50 ounces would be valid. The program compares 50 to the daily goal of 64 ounces and displays a message telling the user they did not meet their goal.

questions.stimulus: A student created a program that helps users track their daily water intake. The program accepts the number of ounces of water the user drank as input and displays a message telling the user whether they met their daily goal of 64 ounces.
questions.question: Identify one unexpected or invalid input a user could provide to this program. Describe the behavior of the program after it receives this input.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for identifying an unexpected or invalid input (e.g. a negative number, a letter, an extremely large number, leaving the field empty).
Award 1 point for describing plausible program behavior after receiving this input (e.g. the program crashes, displays an error message, treats the input as 0, or produces an incorrect result).
Example: A user could enter a negative number like -10. The program may not handle this case and could incorrectly display that the user did not meet their goal, or it may crash if the program does not validate input.

questions.stimulus: A student created a program that helps users track their daily water intake. The program accepts the number of ounces of water the user drank as input and displays a message telling the user whether they met their daily goal of 64 ounces.
questions.question: Identify an example output of this program. Explain how this output shows an aspect of the program's functionality.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for identifying a valid output (e.g. 'You met your goal!', 'You did not meet your goal today.', a message displaying the number of ounces remaining).
Award 1 point for explaining how the output demonstrates functionality — it shows that the program processes the user's input and uses it to determine and communicate whether the daily hydration goal was achieved.
Example: An output of 'You met your goal!' shows that the program successfully compared the user's input to the 64 ounce goal and determined the user drank enough water.

questions.stimulus: Describe one piece of documentation that would be appropriate to include with or in a program. Explain how this documentation can be used by another programmer to better understand a particular code segment in the program.
questions.question: Describe one piece of documentation that would be appropriate to include with or in a program. Explain how this documentation can be used by another programmer to better understand a particular code segment in the program.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for describing a valid piece of documentation. Accept any of the following: a comment describing what a procedure does, a comment explaining what a code segment accomplishes, external documentation describing the program's purpose, an acknowledgement of code from another source.
Award 1 point for explaining how it helps another programmer understand a specific code segment. The explanation must connect the documentation to improved understanding.
Example: A comment placed above a procedure that describes what the procedure does, what parameters it takes, and what it returns would be appropriate documentation. Another programmer could read this comment to understand how to call the procedure and what to expect as output without having to read through all the code inside it.

questions.question:
Part A: Consider the first selection statement in this procedure. Identify the Boolean expression in this selection statement. Identify a specific value or set of values for score and totalPoints that will cause this expression to evaluate to false. Explain why these values cause the expression to evaluate to false.

Part B: Describe the functionality provided by the calculateGrade procedure. Explain how implementing this functionality as a procedure makes the program easier to maintain than if the functionality were not implemented as a procedure.

Part C: Suppose another programmer modifies the procedure by changing the first IF condition from percentage >= 90 to percentage > 90. Describe how this modification would result in a logic error. Explain how the behavior of the procedure would change.
questions.rubric:
PART A (2 points):
Award 1 point for correctly identifying the Boolean expression: percentage >= 90
Award 1 point for identifying values that make it false AND explaining why. Example: score = 75, totalPoints = 100 gives percentage = 75, which is less than 90, so the expression evaluates to false.

PART B (2 points):
Award 1 point for describing the procedure's functionality: it takes a score and total points, calculates a percentage, and displays a letter grade based on that percentage.
Award 1 point for explaining maintainability: if the grading logic needs to change, the programmer only needs to update the procedure in one place rather than changing every place the logic appears in the program.

PART C (2 points):
Award 1 point for describing the logic error: a student who earns exactly 90% would no longer receive an A.
Award 1 point for explaining the behavior change: the procedure now requires strictly greater than 90% to display A, incorrectly assigning a B to students who earned exactly 90%.

questions.stimulus: A team of developers is building a mental health app intended to help teenagers manage stress. The app is built entirely by adult developers with no background in mental health and no input from teenagers during development.
questions.question: Identify the expected group of users of this program. Explain how the development team's approach may affect the program's ability to address the concerns or interests of those users.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for correctly identifying the expected users: teenagers experiencing stress.
Award 1 point for explaining how the team's approach affects the program — the lack of input from teenagers and mental health professionals means the app may not reflect the actual concerns, interests, or needs of its intended users. Diverse perspectives during development help avoid bias and produce innovations that fully incorporate user perspectives.
Example: The expected users are teenagers managing stress. Because the team did not consult with teenagers or mental health professionals during development, the app may not address the concerns that are most relevant to teenagers — it may include features that adults assume are helpful but that teenagers find unhelpful or irrelevant.

questions.stimulus:
A programmer is developing a task management app. While writing the code, they add the following line above one of their procedures:

# Sorting algorithm adapted from merge sort implementation
# by T. Williams, available at opensourcecode.org
questions.question: Explain why the programmer included this line in their code. Describe what information should be included in an acknowledgement of code written by someone else.
questions.rubric:
Award 1 point for explaining why the acknowledgement was included: it is important to acknowledge any code segments that were developed by another source. Using code written by someone else without acknowledgement is a form of plagiarism.
Award 1 point for describing what the acknowledgement should include: the origin of the code and the name of the original author. The response should note both elements.
Example: The programmer included this line because it is important to acknowledge code that was written by someone else. The acknowledgement correctly identifies the origin (opensourcecode.org) and the original author (T. Williams), which is the information required when acknowledging code from another source.
